questions.q: What does Berger say is the most powerful marketing tool?
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that sharing between people, not formal online marketing, is what makes ideas and products spread.

questions.q: What share of word-of-mouth sharing happens online, according to the summary?
questions.why: The summary says only 7 percent of sharing happens online, while 93 percent comes from face-to-face interaction.

questions.q: Why is a friend's recommendation so effective?
a: We trust peers more, and their advice is well targeted
Friends are paid to promote the products they mention
Friends simply repeat the ads they saw online
Friends recommend everything they happen to try
questions.why: Lesson 1 says we trust our peers more than advertisers, and a friend usually recommends something that fits our needs.

questions.q: What made the song Friday and the Geico camel spread so widely?
a: A weekly cue that brought them to mind on certain days
A catchy tune performed by professional singers
questions.why: Lesson 2 shows both spread far more on Fridays and Wednesdays because the day itself triggered people to remember them.

questions.q: Why do stories make ideas stick, according to the summary?
a: They carry a message we absorb without noticing
They present facts in a clear, ordered list
They are shorter than most other content
questions.why: Lesson 3 says stories smuggle a moral beneath the events, so we take it in while focused on the plot.
